Apple___Apple_scab.description: Apple scab is a common fungal disease that affects leaves, fruits, and young shoots. It thrives in cool, wet conditions and can significantly reduce fruit quality and yield if left unmanaged.
symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown spots on leaves
treatment: Remove infected leaves and fallen debris.
Prune trees to improve air circulation.
Apply recommended fungicides during the growing season.
prevention: Use resistant apple varieties whenever possible.
chemical_control: Use registered fungicides according to local agricultural recommendations.
Rotate fungicides with different modes of action to reduce resistance.
farmer_tips: Collect and destroy fallen infected leaves every season.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Black rot is a destructive fungal disease affecting leaves, fruits, and branches. It can reduce yield considerably when environmental conditions favor fungal development.
symptoms: Purple leaf spots with brown centers
organic_control: Use approved organic fungicides where suitable.
chemical_control: Apply registered fungicides during susceptible growth stages.
Follow local extension recommendations.
farmer_tips: Never leave infected fruits on trees.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Cedar apple rust is a fungal disease requiring both apple and juniper hosts to complete its life cycle. It primarily affects leaves and fruits.
symptoms: Bright yellow or orange leaf spots
treatment: Remove nearby infected juniper hosts if practical.
Apply preventive fungicides during early infection periods.
chemical_control: Apply preventive fungicides before infection periods according to local recommendations.
farmer_tips: Avoid planting susceptible apple trees close to infected junipers.

Apple___healthy.description: The leaf appears healthy with no visible symptoms of disease or significant pest damage.
organic_control: Maintain healthy soil using organic matter.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.
farmer_tips: Monitor weather conditions that favor disease development.

Blueberry___healthy.description: The blueberry leaf appears healthy with no visible signs of disease, nutrient deficiency, or pest damage.
prevention: Monitor plants regularly for early disease detection.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: Powdery mildew is a fungal disease that produces white powder-like fungal growth on leaves and young shoots. Severe infections can reduce plant vigor and fruit quality.
organic_control: Use neem oil according to recommendations.
chemical_control: Apply registered fungicides following agricultural guidelines.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: The cherry leaf appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms or pest infestation.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Gray leaf spot is one of the most economically important fungal diseases of corn. It develops rapidly under warm, humid conditions and can significantly reduce grain yield.
treatment: Apply recommended fungicides during early infection.
organic_control: Incorporate crop residues into soil after harvest.
chemical_control: Apply registered foliar fungicides according to local agricultural recommendations.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Common rust is a fungal disease that produces reddish-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces. Severe infections may reduce plant vigor and yield.
treatment: Apply fungicides if disease pressure is high.
organic_control: Promote healthy plant growth through proper nutrient management.
chemical_control: Use registered fungicides when economically justified.
farmer_tips: Take action early if infection spreads rapidly.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Northern leaf blight is a major fungal disease of maize characterized by large cigar-shaped lesions. Severe infections reduce photosynthesis and significantly decrease grain yield.
symptoms: Lesions turn tan as they mature
treatment: Apply recommended foliar fungicides when disease pressure is high.
organic_control: Destroy infected plant debris after harvest.
chemical_control: Use registered fungicides following local agricultural recommendations.
farmer_tips: Scout fields regularly after rainy periods.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: The corn plant appears healthy with normal green leaves and no visible disease symptoms.
organic_control: Maintain healthy soil through organic amendments.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.

Grape___Black_rot.description: Black rot is a destructive fungal disease affecting grape leaves, shoots, and berries. It develops rapidly under warm, humid conditions.
treatment: Apply fungicides during the growing season.
chemical_control: Use registered fungicides according to local recommendations.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Esca is a complex grapevine trunk disease that reduces vine productivity and may eventually kill infected plants.
organic_control: Maintain vine vigor through proper management.
chemical_control: No fully curative chemical treatment is available; follow regional recommendations for pruning wound protection.
farmer_tips: Protect pruning wounds immediately after pruning.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Leaf blight affects grape foliage, reducing photosynthesis and weakening vine growth during favorable environmental conditions.
chemical_control: Apply registered fungicides according to agricultural recommendations.

Grape___healthy.description: The grape leaf appears healthy with no visible signs of disease or nutrient deficiency.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Huanglongbing (HLB), also known as citrus greening, is one of the most destructive citrus diseases. It is transmitted primarily by the Asian citrus psyllid and has no known cure once a tree is infected.
treatment: Remove severely infected trees to reduce disease spread.
Control psyllid populations using integrated pest management.
organic_control: Monitor and reduce psyllid populations using approved biological methods.
chemical_control: Apply registered insecticides for psyllid management following local agricultural recommendations.
farmer_tips: Report suspected infections to local agricultural authorities.
Never propagate trees from infected plants.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot is a destructive disease affecting peach leaves, twigs, and fruits. Warm, humid conditions favor disease development, resulting in reduced fruit quality and yield.
prevention: Prune trees to improve air circulation.
chemical_control: Apply copper-based bactericides or other registered products according to local agricultural recommendations.

Peach___healthy.description: The peach plant appears healthy with vigorous growth and no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot is a serious disease of pepper causing leaf spots, fruit lesions, and yield reduction under warm, wet conditions.
organic_control: Apply approved copper-based products where appropriate.
chemical_control: Use registered bactericides following local agricultural recommendations.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: The pepper plant appears healthy with normal foliage and no visible disease symptoms.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Early blight is a common fungal disease of potato causing significant yield losses, especially in older plants and under warm conditions.
chemical_control: Apply registered fungicides according to agricultural recommendations.
farmer_tips: Avoid leaving infected debris in the field.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Late blight is one of the most devastating potato diseases. Under cool and humid conditions it spreads rapidly and can destroy entire fields within days.
chemical_control: Use registered fungicides following local agricultural recommendations.
farmer_tips: Scout fields daily during humid weather.

Potato___healthy.description: The potato plant appears healthy with vigorous foliage and no visible symptoms of disease.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.

Raspberry___healthy.description: The raspberry plant appears healthy with normal foliage and vigorous growth.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.

Soybean___healthy.description: The soybean plant appears healthy with vigorous growth and no visible signs of disease, nutrient deficiency, or pest infestation.
organic_control: Maintain healthy soil with organic matter.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.
farmer_tips: Rotate crops to preserve soil health.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: Powdery mildew is a common fungal disease that affects squash leaves, reducing photosynthesis and weakening plant growth if left unmanaged.
organic_control: Use neem oil according to label recommendations.
chemical_control: Apply registered fungicides following agricultural recommendations.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Leaf scorch is a fungal disease that causes reddish-purple spots on strawberry leaves, eventually reducing plant vigor and fruit yield.
chemical_control: Use registered fungicides according to local recommendations.

Strawberry___healthy.description: The strawberry plant appears healthy with normal foliage and vigorous growth.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot is a serious disease affecting tomato leaves, stems, and fruits. It spreads rapidly under warm and humid conditions.
organic_control: Apply approved copper-based products where appropriate.
chemical_control: Use registered bactericides following local agricultural recommendations.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Early blight is a common fungal disease of tomato that causes characteristic concentric lesions on leaves, reducing plant vigor and fruit production.
symptoms: Brown circular lesions with concentric rings
chemical_control: Apply registered fungicides according to local recommendations.
farmer_tips: Water at the base of the plant.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Late blight is one of the most destructive diseases of tomato. Under cool and humid conditions it spreads rapidly and can destroy an entire crop within a few days if not managed promptly.
symptoms: White fungal growth on leaf undersides
treatment: Apply recommended fungicides at early stages.
Improve field drainage and air circulation.
chemical_control: Apply registered fungicides according to local agricultural recommendations.
farmer_tips: Scout fields daily during humid weather.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Leaf mold is a fungal disease commonly found in greenhouse and humid environments. Severe infections reduce photosynthesis and overall crop productivity.
symptoms: Yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces
Olive-green mold on lower leaf surfaces
chemical_control: Use registered fungicides according to agricultural recommendations.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Septoria leaf spot is a common fungal disease that primarily affects older tomato leaves, reducing plant vigor and fruit yield.
chemical_control: Apply registered fungicides according to local recommendations.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Two-spotted spider mites are tiny sap-feeding pests that damage tomato leaves, reducing photosynthesis and weakening plants under hot, dry conditions.
organic_control: Use insecticidal soap or neem oil according to recommendations.
chemical_control: Use registered miticides according to local agricultural recommendations.
farmer_tips: Avoid excessive pesticide use that harms beneficial insects.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Target spot is a fungal disease that affects tomato leaves, stems, and fruits. Severe infections reduce photosynthesis, weaken plants, and lower fruit yield.
symptoms: Circular brown lesions with concentric rings
treatment: Improve air circulation within the crop.
Apply recommended fungicides when disease pressure is high.
organic_control: Apply approved biological fungicides where appropriate.
chemical_control: Use registered fungicides according to local agricultural recommendations.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus is one of the most destructive viral diseases of tomato. It is primarily transmitted by whiteflies and can cause severe yield losses.
treatment: There is no cure for infected plants.
prevention: Use resistant tomato varieties where available.
Remove weeds that may act as virus hosts.
organic_control: Use yellow sticky traps for whiteflies.
Apply neem oil according to recommendations.
chemical_control: Apply registered insecticides for whitefly management following local agricultural recommendations.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Tomato Mosaic Virus is a contagious viral disease that spreads through infected plant material, contaminated tools, and human handling. It reduces plant vigor and fruit quality.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves
treatment: There is no cure for infected plants.
Disinfect tools after handling infected plants.
prevention: Avoid tobacco contamination during field work.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is available for viral infections.
farmer_tips: Avoid handling healthy plants after infected ones.
Purchase certified seeds from reliable suppliers.

Tomato___healthy.description: The tomato plant appears healthy with vigorous growth, uniform green foliage, and no visible signs of disease, pest infestation, or nutrient deficiency.
chemical_control: No chemical treatment is necessary.
